description: Dynamic plugin loading system for attack modules. Replace the static imports in orchestrator.py with a plugin discovery/registration system that can load attack modules dynamically from a plugins directory or from the existing posframework/ modules.
steps: Create posframework/plugin_loader.py with a PluginLoader class that: (a) defines a base AttackPlugin abstract class with methods: name(), description(), setup(config), execute(context), teardown(), (b) discovers plugins from a configurable directory (default: posframework/plugins/ and any user-specified path), (c) loads Python modules dynamically using importlib, (d) registers plugins by category (recon, deauth, mitm, dos, printer, etc.), (e) provides get_plugin(name), get_plugins_by_category(category), list_plugins() methods, (f) supports enabling/disabling plugins via configuration.

Create example wrapper plugins in posframework/plugins/ that wrap existing attack modules to demonstrate the plugin interface. Create at least: plugins/deauth_plugin.py (wraps DeauthEngine), plugins/dos_plugin.py (wraps WiFiDoSEngine), plugins/mitm_plugin.py (wraps MITMEngine). Each plugin class inherits from AttackPlugin and delegates to the existing engine.

Refactor posframework/orchestrator.py to use PluginLoader: keep the existing static imports as fallback, but add a load_plugins() method that discovers available plugins and uses them if present. The orchestrator should check for plugins first, fall back to direct imports. Add a 'plugins' parameter to AttackOrchestrator.__init__ that accepts a list of plugin names to enable.
Update posframework/__main__.py to add a --plugins-dir CLI argument and a --list-plugins flag that shows available plugins.
Update posframework/__init__.py to export PluginLoader and AttackPlugin.
acceptance_criteria: posframework/plugin_loader.py exists with PluginLoader and AttackPlugin classes
posframework/plugins/ directory exists with __init__.py and at least 3 example plugins
Each plugin implements the AttackPlugin interface (name, description, setup, execute, teardown)
PluginLoader can discover and load plugins from the plugins directory
AttackOrchestrator has a load_plugins() method and accepts a plugins parameter
Running 'python -c "from posframework.plugin_loader import PluginLoader, AttackPlugin"' succeeds
verification: python -c "from posframework.plugin_loader import PluginLoader, AttackPlugin; print('Plugin system imported OK')"
python -c "from posframework import PluginLoader; loader = PluginLoader(); plugins = loader.list_plugins(); print(f'Found {len(plugins)} plugins')"
